title: Researcher or academic
summary: A compact research index: explain the question, show selected publications with context, and link to the complete scholarly record.

cards.purpose: Explain the research question and affiliation before the specialist record.
Three or four selected papers with authors, venue, year and contribution.
Official openings and collaboration enquiries, if current.
The complete scholarly record and identifiers.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji. This appears in the About popover, not beside the name; repeat the essential purpose in the first text card.

slots.ask: What do you study, in a sentence a curious non-specialist would understand? What is your position and group?
slots.write: One plain-language paragraph, then bold-labelled affiliation and group lines exactly as the institution lists them. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Which three or four publications should visitors see first? Share their titles, authors, venue, year, DOI or link, and a plain-language line about each contribution.
slots.write: tag = venue and year, or Preprint and year; title exactly as published; description = authors in the venue’s order plus a one-line contribution supplied by the researcher, within 300 characters. Use their DOI or publication link. Keep the full record behind a scholarly-profile link; never invent missing bibliographic details. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What should people know before taking this action: who it is for, format, timing, price or reply expectations, only if you want to publish them?
slots.write: One or two short sentences, at most 400 characters. Include only facts supplied for this action; do not assume an introductory call is free or that any date, price or reply time is current. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Are you recruiting students or postdocs, or open to collaboration?
slots.write: Text = what is open and from when, as on the official advert. Institutional email only if they want it shown. Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What short heading should introduce this action?
slots.write: Use a clear heading that describes the action; no unconfirmed availability or promise. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Which scholarly profiles should be linked: ORCID, Google Scholar, institutional page, code?
slots.write: Profile URLs only. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Any talks or courses you want to list?
slots.write: tag = type · year; title as given; description = event and city. Select up to four featured entries for this page; link to the complete archive or catalogue instead of deleting the person’s remaining work. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a photo, artwork or logo you want to upload as the profile picture?
slots.write: The person uploads their chosen picture in the editor. Never fetch, generate or infer a personal photo. Use their description for alt text wherever the editor asks for it.
